brief: Deutsche Bank's daily macro note frames markets as subdued into today's US September CPI print amid three crosscurrents: a chip selloff extending to a 5th session on AI fears, mixed US bank earnings (JPM and GS missed on fixed-income trading, Citi's stock fell most despite a beat), and rising oil prices reviving inflation fears. Oil's run-up pushed October Fed hike odds back to 24%, the highest since October 1, reversing doubt created by a weak jobs report and French political stress. DB expects headline CPI at +0.57% month-on-month (+3.6% year-on-year, highest since May), driven by a +9.6% jump in motor fuel prices, but a softer core reading of +0.16% month-on-month (+2.4% year-on-year). Either surprise matters because PCE, the Fed's preferred gauge, does not print until after the next meeting. Williams backs one more hike this year and no more. Barkin wants the Fed to grow more restrictive. Front-end yields rose on the hawkish tone while the long end fell on a risk-off bid. CoreWeave's credit default swap widened sharply amid the AI-driven selloff. Overnight, China's CPI came in soft, PPI came in hot, and trade data beat broadly as Asian chipmakers rebounded.
